Underscoring the PBBM ADMIN’s push for stronger disaster resilience, President @bongbongmarcos on August 11, 2025, personally inspected the Pasig–Marikina River Channel Improvement Project (PMRCIP) Phase IV at the Marikina Bridge Under Loop in Barangay Sto. Niño, Marikina City.

Implemented by the Department of Public Works and Highways (DPWH) in collaboration with the Japan International Cooperation Agency (JICA), the initiative is part of a multi-phase flood control strategy designed to address one of Metro Manila’s most persistent problems - the overflow of the Pasig and Marikina Rivers during heavy rains and typhoons.

Phase IV is notable for combining structural solutions such as the construction of reinforced dikes and revetments, the installation of modern floodgates, and large-scale dredging operations with non-structural measures like improved river monitoring and management. The integrated approach aims not only to protect lives and property, but also to enable sustainable urban development along vulnerable waterways.

Covering critical sections of the National Capital Region, the project is expected to reduce the frequency and severity of flooding in both Metro Manila and surrounding areas. Contract Package 3, which Marcos inspected, is a flagship infrastructure component funded through bilateral agreements with Japan-reflecting the Philippines’ growing emphasis on climate adaptation partnerships with international allies.

According to DPWH, the completion of this phase will strengthen the region’s flood management network, safeguard key economic hubs, and improve the quality of life for thousands of residents living in flood-prone communities.

PBBM | #SalamatPBBM | #BuildBetterMore | #MarcosPaRin | #BagongPilipinas | #PBBMgoodnews |
